title: Anki Miner Android AnkiDroid callback payloads
$comment: Every callback is synchronous and returns an envelope. anki_limits_v1.json is the exact cross-language resource manifest: JSON Schema maxLength counts Unicode scalar values, while Python and Kotlin independently enforce its UTF-8 byte and complete-envelope byte ceilings before provider access or JSON decoding. Before JSON decoding both runtimes apply the 1000-character lexical number-token ceiling with a string-aware scanner/tokenizer. Contract Unicode decisions use the generated Unicode 15.1/Python 3.13 helpers, never host normalization or whitespace tables. Responses repeat runId/requestId; media and note results are positionally aligned with requests. EpisodeProcessor verifies the target before mining; create_cards_batch then uses that cached ordered field model to preflight the complete create call before progress, media hashing, or any create-phase provider callback at 2000 source items, 16 MiB source UTF-8, 16 MiB built-note UTF-8 including worst-case provider filename rewrites, 8000 media references, and 512 MiB of actual streamed media work shared by every card and dictionary digest. verifyTarget validates bounded model/deck names, standard model type 0, 1 through 64 templates/cards per note, and at most 64 bounded model fields before deck creation; its ordered fieldNames[0] is the duplicate identity for the run. Before deck creation Kotlin also bounds provider-owned CSS, LaTeX pre/post, and every question/answer/browser template body at 262144 UTF-8 bytes each and their complete snapshot at 4194304 UTF-8 bytes; these are local generated limits and are not caller-negotiable fields. Duplicate scans are bounded candidate-key lookups, never full-model scans. Kotlin returns raw provider first fields and Python alone applies the desktop duplicate normalizer. Duplicate baselines, known-vocabulary cursors, media acknowledgements, provider staging, and reconciliation metadata are bounded, opaque, run-scoped Kotlin state. Every note explicitly carries mediaBindings derived by Python from prepared media provenance and the materialized note; Kotlin validates them against same-live-run acknowledgements and never parses note markup. Under one registry lock, releaseRunState sets sticky releaseRequested and rejects new operations. acknowledgeTerminalResponses is true only after Python fully decoded and semantically accepted every terminal mutation response; failure is sticky and the callback-independent fallback is false. Live reads, staging jobs, or writes keep the entire run quarantined and return deferred. Each task reconciles and releases resources outside the lock while still registered; before the last task deregisters, it registers exactly one cleanup task. Cleanup runs outside the lock and only then atomically removes and unquarantines the run. A no-owner release completes the same registered-cleanup sequence synchronously. Missing or already-finalized state is absent, with no Anki-registry tombstone and no lazy run recreation. The Kotlin coordinator invokes this same request-release transition in finally as a callback-independent fallback, never unconditional deletion. AndroidAnkiAdapter.close accepts every terminal disposition and suppresses cleanup failures. Release itself performs no provider mutation. Every card and dictionary asset is Python-stat-gated at 64 MiB and streamed through cancellable SHA-1/SHA-256 hashing before provider mutation; sourcePath is absolute, NUL-free, and at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; each media callback is bounded to 50 assets and 64 MiB total. Kotlin must stream sourcePath into a private bounded snapshot, reject unless its byte count and SHA-256 exactly match the expected values, then expose only that snapshot to AnkiDroid. A stored result means the provider-returned filename has a safely proven postcondition; uncertain means the insert may have committed without a proven filename and forbids blind retry. preferredName is the safe extensionless prefix required by AnkiDroid addMediaFromUri; requestedFilename preserves the exact direct-fallback basename; actualFilename is a raw basename, never [sound:] or markup, and Python rewrites marked dictionary HTML to the provider-returned name. Runtime validation additionally enforces encoded UTF-8 filename limits, aggregate duplicate-hit and note UTF-8/item/envelope budgets including both binding values, provider-name relationships and collisions, unique positive note IDs, and strict terminal-failure/notAttempted ordering with top-level errors.

canonicalNonEmptyString.$comment: Runtime validation additionally enforces NFC and rejects every Unicode category-C code point.

filename.$comment: Runtime validation additionally caps encoded UTF-8 length at 1024 bytes, enforces NFC and bare-basename semantics, and rejects every Unicode category-C code point.

mediaBasename.$comment: Exact media basename used by the direct-name fallback. Runtime validation caps encoded UTF-8 length at 1024 bytes and rejects slash, backslash, dot-segments, and every Unicode category-C code point; valid Yomitan names may contain quotes, brackets, spaces, and non-NFC text.

allOf.$comment: A callback returns the raw filename, never Anki field markup.

mediaBinding.$comment: Python emits this only from prepared-media provenance after proving the exact acknowledged filename is referenced by the complete materialized note. Kotlin validates the exact pair against this still-live run and never parses fields or markup.

firstField.$comment: Exact built first-field value. Kotlin computes AnkiDroid's field checksum from this value and returns the bounded raw provider hits. The key is an opaque Python-normalized identity; Kotlin must not normalize or compare against it.

key.$comment: Opaque Python-normalized identity included for positional auditability. Kotlin must not normalize or interpret it.

firstField.$comment: Exact verified model first field whose AnkiDroid checksum selects the provider note-ID snapshot. The baseline IDs remain private Kotlin state behind baselineToken.

occurrence.$comment: Zero-based ordered probe occurrence. Values in createNotes are unique and strictly increasing; Kotlin verifies the candidate at each occurrence against the token-bound occurrence map, preventing replay or fan-out of repeated candidates.

requiredFields.$comment: Runtime aggregate maximum is 16384 UTF-8 bytes.

verifyTargetResult.$comment: ContentProvider verifyTarget may durably create or reconcile a missing deck within the callback, but always reports deckCreated=false because provider observations cannot prove creator ownership across same-name races. If entered creation cannot be conclusively reconciled to one non-dynamic target deck, it returns an anki.error with post_commit_uncertain and retryable=false rather than a result or blind retry.

fieldNames.$comment: Runtime aggregate maximum is 16384 UTF-8 bytes. Kotlin rejects a wider target before deck creation or any later provider operation.

knownVocabularyScope.$comment: Kotlin scans at most maxScannedNotes notes per page and pages by ascending note ID, so a traversal has no total note ceiling and a collection cannot be too large to scan. An excluded deck excludes the entire note when any of its cards is in that deck or a descendant; a parent exclusion therefore covers all subdecks. cursor is null on the first page and otherwise exactly the prior nextCursor. Kotlin retains the resume point and immutable run/scope/ordinal binding behind each opaque one-use token; tokens expire when consumed, on terminal completion, on error, or when the run is cancelled/terminated. A cursor from another run or scope and a replay fail closed. Kotlin must fail rather than truncate or skip an oversized first field.

excludedDecks.$comment: Runtime aggregate maximum is 65536 UTF-8 bytes.

token.$comment: Opaque, one-use provider continuation capability bound to the originating run, immutable scan scope, next ordinal, and the note ID the traversal resumes after. Runtime validation caps encoded UTF-8 length at 1024 bytes.

duplicateScope.$comment: firstFieldName must exactly equal fieldNames[0] from this run's verified model snapshot. Kotlin atomically invalidates invalidateBaselineToken, if non-null and owned by this run, before retaining the fresh replacement baselineToken. At most one unconsumed duplicate baseline may exist per run: createNotes consumes it once, the next sequential duplicate probe invalidates an abandoned all-duplicate token, and run cancellation/termination performs final cleanup. A mismatched invalidation token fails closed.

occurrences.$comment: Ordered occurrence-to-candidate indexes for the original Python batch. This preserves repeated candidate multiplicity while candidates remains a bounded unique lookup set.

invalidateBaselineToken.$comment: Null on the first probe or immediately after a consumed createNotes token; otherwise exactly the run's sole outstanding token from the preceding all-duplicate probe.

baselineToken.$comment: Fresh, opaque and run-bound. Kotlin alone retains the complete provider note-ID baseline and accepts this token for at most one createNotes callback.

rawFirstFieldHits.$comment: Outer entries are positionally aligned with duplicateScope.candidates. Kotlin queries note IDs plus raw first fields by the checksum of each exact firstField and, when deckName is non-null, retains only notes with a card in that exact deck (never children). Note IDs are unique within each bucket. Kotlin must fail instead of truncating when any requested limit would be exceeded; Python validates every limit again and owns all HTML/media/entity/NFC/whitespace normalization. Provider note IDs never round-trip through createNotes; Kotlin binds them privately to baselineToken.

sourcePath.$comment: Absolute POSIX path. NUL and UTF-16 surrogate code points are forbidden; the runtime maximum is 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

preferredName.$comment: Safe extensionless addMediaFromUri prefix; dictionary media uses a deterministic digest alias.

requestedFilename.$comment: Exact full basename required by a direct-name media fallback. Card assets use safe content-addressed names; dictionary assets preserve valid Yomitan basenames.

uncertainMedia.$comment: The provider mutation may have committed but no safe actual filename/postcondition can be proven. The top-level error code is post_commit_uncertain with retryable=false and every later row is notAttempted.

storeMediaResult.$comment: Rows are request-aligned. uncertain ends provider attempts, requires post_commit_uncertain with retryable=false, and may be the only or final row; every later row is notAttempted. notAttempted forms a strict suffix and requires a top-level error. Callback-wide anki.error is valid only before this callback's first possible provider mutation. A provider-wide stop after a possible mutation must use this aligned result shape so Python retains every known stored filename and explicit uncertainty. If any row is stored and a top-level error is present, retryable must be false. Row-local failed semantics are unchanged and remain degradable only for media_store_failed. Retry is allowed only when Kotlin proves no provider mutation occurred or verifies the desired postcondition.

createNotesLimits.$comment: All byte limits are exact encoded UTF-8 counts. note content is the sum of field-name, field-value, tag, media-binding assetId, and media-binding actualFilename bytes. envelope is the complete canonical bridge JSON envelope. Kotlin validates every declared constant before parsing provider-bound values and rejects rather than truncating.

createNotesRequest.$comment: Kotlin atomically consumes baselineToken only when its run/model/verified firstFieldName/candidate/scope binding exactly matches this request. It resolves every candidate's scoped checksum note IDs before inserting any note. A note is duplicate iff that immutable pre-insert snapshot contains an ID absent from the private baseline. maxTotalNoteIds counts the union of IDs across candidates. Kotlin fails rather than truncating on every declared limit and must never add IDs created by this same request to the snapshot. A new checksum collision may safely false-positive; a new external note must never false-negative. Callback-wide anki.error is valid only before any provider mutation. After a possible mutation Kotlin returns an aligned result, preserves every known inserted noteId, and uses a non-retryable uncertain row when commit state cannot be proven. Blind write retry is forbidden.

failedNote.$comment: The provider proved that this note was not committed. This row ends attempts; every later row is notAttempted.

committedFailedNote.$comment: The note was inserted and its ID is known, but a required post-insert routing or verification step failed. Python retains noteId. The top-level error is non-retryable and every later row is notAttempted.

uncertainNote.$comment: A provider mutation may have committed but no safe note ID/postcondition can be proven. The top-level error code is post_commit_uncertain with retryable=false and every later row is notAttempted.

createNotesResult.$comment: Rows are request-aligned. failed, committedFailed, uncertain, or notAttempted requires a top-level error and ends attempts; notAttempted is a strict suffix. Any known created/committed note IDs are retained. An error after any provider mutation is never retryable. Cancellation observed after a possible commit is post_commit_uncertain, not a clean cancelled result.

releaseRunStateRequest.$comment: Idempotent run-finalization command. Coordinator admission is separate from the Anki state registry: handlers never lazily create an unknown/finalized run. Under the registry lock this command sets sticky releaseRequested on a live run, so every new operation fails closed. All registered reads, local-staging jobs, and writes remain owners until they reconcile, close cursors, revoke URI grants, and delete task staging outside the registry lock. If an owner remains, the complete run state stays quarantined and the command returns deferred. Before the last owner deregisters under the lock, it registers one cleanup task; that task releases remaining resources outside the lock, then atomically removes the run and unquarantines it. With no owner, this command follows the same registered-cleanup sequence synchronously. Cleanup is exactly once, finalized run objects are removed, and later release returns absent without retaining an Anki-registry tombstone or permitting run recreation. The coordinator's finally block invokes the same transition directly if this callback fails. The transition itself performs no ContentProvider mutation.

releaseRunStateResult.$comment: released means this request atomically finalized retained state. deferred means releaseRequested is sticky but at least one provider task still owns quarantined state; repeated release remains deferred until exactly-once task finalization. absent means no state exists or deferred cleanup already finalized. Every state is a successful, idempotent acknowledgement.
